title: Resolving Representation Ambiguity in Feedforward Novel View Synthesis Transformer via Semantic-Spatial Decoupling
claim: Separating semantic and spatial representations yields structured, object-aligned features, while the mixed baseline gives blurry, lattice-like features.
layout: 3 rows by 5 columns, input then variants left-to-right, PCA feature maps
description: A grid of three indoor scenes, one per row. The first column shows the input photo: a dining room, a kitchen doorway and a bedroom with a sea view. The next four columns show false-color feature maps from middle layers of the model. Column (a) is the baseline, with blurry, blocky color patches and a faint grid pattern. Column (b) adds decoupling, and the maps show sharper structure: windows, doors and furniture become recognizable. Column (c) adds supervision and modulation to (a), which gives noisy, speckled pixels. Column (d) adds supervision and modulation to (b), and the maps are crisp and coherent, matching the scene layout. Column headers are plain text. The eye goes first to the saturated colors and the contrast between the blurry (a) column and the structured (b) and (d) columns.
caption: Feature Map Comparison across Model Variants. We visualize middle-layer LVSM features: (a) the LVSM baseline; (b) Decouple-only, with separate semantic and spatial branches and no categorized supervision or modulation; (c,d) supervision and modulation added to (a,b), respectively. Decoupling produces more structured representations and enables the auxiliary designs.
abstract: Transformer-based models have advanced feedforward novel view synthesis (NVS). Current architectures such as GS-LRM and LVSM mix semantic information (e.g., RGB) and spatial information (e.g., PlÃ¼cker rays) into a shared feature space. Since PlÃ¼cker rays naturally carry lattice-like spatial structure, these designs can make the spatial bias interfere with appearance representation and degrade rendering fidelity. To this end, we propose to decouple the representation of feedforward NVS transformers into separate semantic and spatial tokens. The decoupled design keeps semantic and spatial information explicit in their branches while preserving cross-branch interaction through shared attention routing. Built on this design, we introduce optional categorized supervision and bidirectional modulation: the former provides branch-specific training signals, while the latter improves interaction between the two branches. Notably, the base decoupled design introduces virtually zero additional inference latency due to its architectural design. The proposed designs achieve consistent improvements, demonstrating effectiveness across decoder-only and encoder-decoder feedforward NVS models.
